alternatives.why_less_likely: Orders did retry payments without backoff, but this retry storm was triggered by payments errors; without those errors there would be no amplification.
Orders queueing occurred after payments errors and retries; it is a downstream effect of load amplification, not the initial trigger.

causal_chain.claim: Payments returned errors originating in the service.
Orders scheduled retries to payments with zero backoff.
Orders experienced queueing as workers were busy handling retries.
Gateway timed out waiting for orders.

root_cause.summary: Payments began returning internal errors (temporarily_unavailable), causing callers to see failures.

alternatives.why_less_likely: While payments latency increased, the dominant evidence is worker pool exhaustion and 503 errors, indicating capacity saturation rather than mere slowness.

causal_chain.claim: Payments service experienced capacity saturation, shown by all workers busy and 503 errors.
Orders service retried payments calls immediately (backoff_ms=0) after receiving 503.
The retry amplification increased load on payments, worsening its saturation.
Orders latency rose and gateway observed upstream timeouts waiting for orders.
Gateway experienced high latency and 5xx errors as the timeout propagated outward.

root_cause.summary: Payments exhausted its worker pool (all 12 workers busy), causing 503 responses and increased latency.
